text:
In Sufi tradition, we have a word for this type of apprenticeship, Meshk. It derives from the word Ashk (Love).

Explained beautifully by one my teachers: Meshk is the traditional method by which many forms of arts and crafts are taught and passed from one generation to the next. Grounded in direct, one-to-one communication and interaction between teacher and learner, the system lets the student absorb not only technical skills but also the art’s or craft’s heritage, stylistic nuances, and unwritten codes of conduct.

First, the learner must seek out a teacher and ask to study together. The teacher, in turn, must find the learner suitable and agree to accept them. In other words, meshk requires mutual selection. Besides general requirements, a teacher may impose additional conditions unique to his own practice.

Foremost among the universal requirements is Ashk (Love). Success in Meshk rests on intense work and deep concentration. The student must channel all time and energy, day and night, into the practice, clearing heart and mind of everything else. Such total devotion is possible only through unconditional, powerful Ashk. Hence, without Ashk, there can be no Meshk.

Yet Ashk alone is not enough. The learner must also possess keen intelligence, quick comprehension, innate talent, physical aptitude (perhaps even superiority), and agility — everything needed to thrive in Meshk.

Traditionally, Meshk unfolds face-to-face. The teacher explains and demonstrates; the student watches attentively, then imitates. The teacher corrects mistakes. They continue until the learner knows what the teacher knows and can do what the teacher can do. One priceless thing remains: experience — something the learner must cultivate independently afterward.

Beyond skill transfer, Meshk’s deeper role is to carry forward the traditions, styles, and behavioral codes of an art’s or craft’s practitioners. By spending long stretches of time with the teacher, the learner observes, senses, and eventually embodies the teacher’s state of being. States are contagious; they spread. Thus, despite natural changes over time, a core way of perceiving, thinking, feeling, and living is handed down intact from generation to generation.

Meshk is an exceedingly humble practice, revolving around respect and Love. It has a dual nature: the teacher meshks with the learner, and the learner meshks with the teacher — both engage, both evolve. Ultimately, teacher and learner alike become students and practitioners of “the true, absolute and singular Teacher”. 

In Sufism, all forms of Love and selfless devotion, leads to Enlightenment, leads to God.

WHAT?! GOOGLE JUST OPEN-SOURCED SELF-IMPROVING AI AGENTS 🤯

It's called Harness², and it lets agents rewrite their own harnesses to get better at new tasks.

100% open source.

Here's how it works:

1. Propose changes to prompts, tools, memory, skills, and other components
2. Probe each change by running the actual task
3. Compose the best changes into an improved harness

No retraining. No ground-truth answers. Model weights stay frozen.

The clever part?

Each task leaves behind improvements the agent can reuse.

By task 50, it's building on lessons from the previous 49.

Google reports gains of up to 11.8 percentage points after just one refinement step on a legal benchmark.

text:
Token2049 期间，我受邀参加了火币的内部活动，做了一场 panel 分享，也出席了他们的 VIP 晚宴。另外和孙宇晨孙哥@justinsuntron 即兴约了一场采访，目前正在打磨问题。

**先替火币澄清一件事。晚宴原定 6 号，后来因为安排调整改到了 8 号。工作人员是真的尽心尽力，我亲眼看着他们为了协调好每一个人，焦灼地忙了全程。办过活动的人都知道，现场总有太多突发状况：场地临时变更，容纳人数跟着变，这些未知因素导致一些 VIP 没能到场。但团队自始至终都在积极解决问题。

火币的现场活动给我一种很不一样的感觉。在其他交易所的夹击之下，来到现场的反而都是火币多年的老用户，整场氛围其乐融融，非常家人向🙏感谢 @Ceee333_ 的邀请，她是这场活动的负责人之一，也是双语主持，业务能力相当过硬。还有@HTX_Molly @Lumibb_ @Xiaodu_HTX 等火币的小伙伴，每个人都很 energetic。这是我第一次深度接触火币的活动对接团队，评价很高（我不是托，是托死全家）。

**再说说我筹划的这场采访（目前身体太差的确稍微拖延了）。我有稍微看了下孙哥和邵艾伦那场”薄肌”采访，以及和自由潜冠军金明聊 Crypto、AI 与量子威胁的那场。我想问点不太一样的人文向问题，因为我的视角可能有些特别：我是从新概念时期就知道孙哥的。同为新概念作文大赛的获奖者，他某种程度上算是我的前辈。我第一次听到这个名字，是在《萌芽》上读到他写的《一道论证题》，所以对他的文青之路一路追踪非常熟稔。

我也注意到，孙哥提到他们生态里一直比较活跃的以太坊挖矿活动，所以也想专门问问他怎么看 ETH 这个资产。对于BTC被攻破这块，我和以太坊基金会做抗量子研究和在Yale/MIT读相关PHD的一些朋友交流过，他们对 Q-Day 的到来目前还算比较乐观，这个话题也想和他聊聊。

**最后一个小提议：**除了数学奖，火币很值得再设一个文学奖/人文奖。我感觉现在这些交易所办的这种访谈活动，基本上都是跟交易员对谈，来来回回，其实也都是那些交易员，同质化程度太高了，包括打广告的 KOL 也是，基本上是今天做完交易所 A 的广告，明天又去发交易所 B 的广告。孙哥既是新概念出身，又做过社交 App（陪我），某种程度上“薄肌”也算是一种文化输出了，那是否火币可以系统性以活动的形式支持更多元的加密文化输出？

先发散到这儿，抛砖引玉，之后再细聊。

艾伦的内心是崇拜着孙哥的。
就像孙宇晨曾经崇拜着王小川一样。

又崇拜，又想崩偶像一口。

艾伦想蹭孙哥，
但他不知道其实孙哥潜伏在暗处观察他很久了。
这个暗夜的捕食者，早就看准了自己最大的粉丝头子艾伦，需要伺机吃他一口大的。

孙哥看着嫩嫩的艾伦，想起了嫩嫩的自己见王小川时 努力证明自己嫩嫩的窘迫。

视频中，艾伦把头发梳成黄毛模样，努力向孙哥展示薄肌的样子。
就如同孙哥当年竖着小油头跟王小川介绍自己是瑞波大中华区负责人一样。

孙哥没有像王小川当年耿直说他那样说：你是个骗子，你永远不会成功。
深度网络冲浪的孙哥只是笑笑：对对，你说的都对。
递给观众的潜台词就像王思聪当年评价孙哥一样：这不就是个傻逼。

然后孙哥火速推出一条提前演拍剪，精心准备良久的高逼格装逼专访视频，
引导观众高下立判：
哦，原来不是孙哥没水平。是艾伦太傻逼。

孙哥的口碑自此开始逆转，深藏功与名。
无脑慕强男粉开始沸腾了：哇，金明是我们新的男神！！

孙哥视角：
艾伦一届自媒体网红，属于一次性员工，吃完即扔。
金明乃湖畔同学，有人脉社交价值和运动员属性，可以用于赚钱站台，和互相抬咖，属于反复洗涤型员工。

献祭一个一次性员工做顺水人情，帮反复洗涤型员工抬咖 涨慕强男粉，
金明日后无论投资还是带单回人情，都会把这些吃到的慕强男粉价值回归到孙哥业务。

孙哥暗暗想，也许能挽救自己交易场子于水火。

此乃驱金明吞艾伦之计。
与艾伦一起倒塌的，还有薄肌教。
因为薄肌<国家运动员<亚洲纪录保持者。
金明是孙哥刻意挑出来，引群众拉踩宫斗艾伦的。
目的是pua艾伦，将艾伦的自尊心彻底击碎，从而彻底变成孙哥的后宫。

此毒计的受害人除了艾伦，
还有尾端将被变现的艾伦辛苦购买 辛苦经营的慕强男粉们。

此计，

让这个全网以自己一千万粉引以为傲的少年，

变成了全网一千万粉丝心目中的大傻逼🤡

text:
Here's The Real Reason Crypto Has Been Down Lately

We know the macro sucks. But that alone isn't a death sentence. In recent history, we've seen sharp gains across crypto even while the broader macroeconomic environment has been troubling.

No, I believe the primary factor driving the market lower over the past couple of weeks has been the incredible resilience of highly leveraged LONG perpetual futures traders.

With data provided by the engine powering https://t.co/wcD5xzlyfV - which ingests fresh market data approximately four times per second - I've been able to observe a persistent trend over the past week: the overwhelming majority of traders remain long.

One group of longs gets wiped out, and another immediately steps in to replace them.

At the time of this posting:

BTC: 64% long
ETH: 76% long
SOL: 72% long

Across all three assets, there is considerably more liquidation fuel sitting within a 3% move to the downside than within an equivalent 3% move to the upside.

While nothing is ever guaranteed, markets have a tendency to follow the path of least resistance unless there is a catalyst to the other direction.

Furthermore, markets rarely reward the crowded trade.

Despite all the downside we've already experienced, we're still not seeing the kind of capitulation I believe is necessary before the market can establish a sustainable foundation for another move higher.

Every time the market attempts to flush out excessive leverage, another wave of traders rushes in to catch the falling knife. In doing so, they inadvertently create the very conditions that make further downside attractive.

It's a self-perpetuating cycle.

Until that cycle breaks, I believe meaningful upside will remain difficult to obtain.

While I never recommend taking highly leveraged positions, if you're determined to do it anyway, at least consider positioning your liquidation levels 10% or more (on BTC) away from the current price. That doesn't eliminate your risk, but it may reduce your vulnerability to relatively ordinary market movements.

Otherwise, you're simply continuing to provide fuel for the downside.

The irony is that many of the traders desperately trying to position themselves for the next rally are helping prevent it from happening.

Right now, the bears are playing this game considerably smarter than the bulls.

Until that changes, I see little reason to believe the market is finished teaching us this lesson.

🫡 From the depths — 
The White Whale 🐋

text:
Il y aura un avant et un après le 17 octobre 2026.

Qu'on arrête de nous raconter que la jeunesse française s'est soulevée pour une école en panne. C'est faux.

L'immense majorité des lycéens n'était pas dans la rue samedi. Si on lui demandait son avis, elle dirait qu'elle veut étudier, bosser, construire sa vie. La majorité silencieuse ne brûle pas des mairies.

Ce qu'on a vu samedi, ce n'est pas une révolte sociale. C'est une instrumentalisation totale. Des structures radicalisées qui utilisent des gamins de 16 ans comme bouclier moral et des revendications légitimes comme paravent.

Mais il faut comprendre d'où ça vient.

Pendant 20 ans, le bloc central a gouverné main dans la main avec le globalisme bruxellois. Macron, Ursula von der Leyen, la Commission, les mêmes réflexes, le même mépris pour les nations, la même certitude d'avoir raison contre les peuples. Ils ont laissé l'immigration se gérer toute seule. Ils ont laissé l'école s'effondrer. Ils ont laissé la vie devenir hors de prix. Et chaque fois que quelqu'un osait le dire, ils le traitaient de raciste, de facho, d'extrême droite.

Ce système a fabriqué le chaos. Et aujourd'hui, c'est l'extrême gauche qui le récolte.

Voilà l'intrication que personne ne veut nommer. Le centre globaliste a créé le vide. L'extrême gauche s'y est engouffrée, en s'appuyant sur une immigration mal gérée et une jeunesse qu'on a abandonnée. Les deux se détestent en apparence. En réalité, l'un produit les fractures, l'autre les exploite. Et les deux ont un ennemi commun : ceux qui disaient la vérité depuis le début.

Samedi, des millions de Français ont regardé les images. L'hôtel de ville de Limoges en feu. Un poste de police saccagé à Marseille. Des journalistes agressés à Paris. Et ils ont compris : ceux qu'on faisait taire décrivaient simplement la réalité.

C'est pour ça que je suis optimiste.

On est à l'aube d'une prise de conscience globale. Je le dis depuis longtemps : on va vivre un nouveau 1989. Les empires du mensonge ne tombent pas sous les coups. Ils tombent le jour où plus personne n'y croit.

La France tombera la première. Mais elle tombera la première pour se relever la première. La fin du globalisme incarné par Macron et von der Leyen ne sera pas la fin de l'Occident. Ce sera sa renaissance.

Le 17 octobre, quelque chose s'est brisé. Pas la France. Le mensonge.

On s'en souviendra.

text:
《盐卤牛肉》教程，简化版，容易上手，失败率较低！

不废话直接进入正题，此版本盐卤牛肉分为两个部分，腌制与卤制，需要提前1-2天准备，看个人喜好

腌制部分：

一，食材准备与洗净去腥

1，选材三花腱与五花腱都可以，五花口感更好，但是贵点，自己吃追求口感可以选五花，或者好的三花可以。

2，牛肉买回来用“牛肉松肉针”多扎一些孔，或者用竹签或者几根牙签代替，目的是给牛肉多扎一些细小的孔，容易放出血水与后续腌制

3，冷水浸泡2-4个小时，1个小时换一边水，目的是让血水浸泡出去减少血腥味，这一步不可偷懒，否则后续牛肉腥味重，后续浸泡的血水变清澈就好

4，提前一个小时捞出牛肉，控水，让牛肉表面没有多余水分，开始下一步准备腌制。

二，腌料制作

1，盐卤以盐为主，一斤牛肉约15-20克盐，喜欢口重20克/每斤，喜欢口轻10克/每斤。

2，香料配置，北方大姜，不要选小黄姜，切片准备。香料：香叶2-3片捏碎，八角2-3个掰开，桂皮1-2块掰开，花椒30-50克，超过10斤加倍，白芷一片即可，豆蔻有的话放一个没有就算，小茴香可放可不放，放到一个碗里浸泡15分钟更加干净。

3，炒制，目的是让盐高温之后把姜、香料抄干的过程，这样姜与香料的味道会进入盐中，腌制的过程中更加入味。

4，炒盐，小火放入盐，开始炒制，当盐开始微微变黄这时候温度上来了，开始放入姜片，继续小火焙炒。这里需要注意，不要先放姜在放盐，放姜的时候盐一定是高温状态，否则姜片的水分反而会让盐融化，失败。

5，当姜片表面不在粘盐，此时放入洗干净控好水的香料，继续小火焙炒，最后当姜片变干，香料味道被激发，关火盛出来放量备用。

三，腌制

1，准备一个可以放入冰箱冷藏区的容器，开始腌制牛肉

2，控干水分的牛肉开始抹上放量的炒制盐，带上手套好好搓一下，让盐更容易跟牛肉结合，弄好一个放进容器，一次类推。

3，最好炒干的香料在容器底部放一些，剩下的一层牛肉铺一点，保证香料可以入味。

4，保鲜膜封号容易口放入冰箱冷鲜、冷藏即可。

5，腌制24-48小时即可，根据个人口味，如果喜欢更有香料味道跟盐味，放24小时，如果不喜欢，则24小时，期间每12个小时把肉翻一下，让腌制更加充分。

卤制部分：

一，焯水

1，提前将冷鲜的牛肉拿出来令其回归常温，然后洗掉表面多余的香料备用

2，把锅中多加水，保证水漫过牛肉，冷水下锅，开始焯水，只需要放入适量的黄酒、料酒或者高度白酒去腥，其他不用放

3，加热过程一定不要盖盖，大火滚开一直保持，期间有多余的血沫在表面形成用勺子撇掉，这个过程不要偷懒，有了血沫就直接撇掉，一直重复，如果期间水不够了，不要加凉水，加烧开的热水，让水始终保持高于牛肉。

4，当血沫基本没有，汤清亮的时候关火，开始卤制牛肉。这里面汤头有两个选项

a，选用焯水的原汤，牛肉味道重，喜欢牛肉味道的可以直接用
b，不喜欢牛肉味道重的，原汤去掉直接用新的热水来卤制

二，卤制

1，准备大葱一颗切断，葱叶不要，大量生姜切片，50克花椒（牛肉喜花椒），大料2个，香叶两片（不喜欢这个味道减1片），白芷，豆蔻（可选），桂皮1-2个，小茴香（可选），干辣椒（自由选择放不放），冰糖（5-10粒）

2，将香料洗净+葱姜放入料带（各类网购平台都有，买大号），放入冰糖（并且不要洗哈），料包准备完成。

3，将容器中加入热水或者焯水牛肉的原汤，然后加入东古一品（黄豆酱油），借他的酱香，少量生抽调色，此时放冰糖的作用就出来了，中和酱料中的苦味，然后尝一下咸淡，因为我们提前腌制牛肉有基础底味，所以卤制中不要放太多盐，有咸味即可。

三，卤制容器选择，不同卤制时间

1，首选高压锅方便，但是使用危险，没有经验的人慎用，高压锅大火上汽，然后中小火30分钟，北方牛肉更加有韧性可以视情况+10分钟，

2，普通炖煮容器，多加水，炖煮期间不要在增加水，大火烧开，期间不盖盖，水开中小火45分钟，然后用筷子插一下，如果轻松插入，就是熟了，然后关火浸泡2-4个小时自然放凉。如果筷子插不进去，+5分钟炖煮时间，每隔5分钟测试一次。

3，电饭煲，没试过，但是网络上有大把教程，相比高压锅更加安全，好像是45分钟即可，如果觉得不够软肋，同理，关闭电源后用锅中余温浸泡2-4个小时

四，存放

1，牛肉放凉或者放温之后，立马用保鲜膜包括放冰箱，过程包的紧实一点，这样有型且口感更好

2，每个牛腱子包裹好后放入冰箱冷冻，保存，基本可以放很久时间，如果第二天要吃，第一天提前拿出来放到冷鲜上自然解冻，吃的时候直接切片就可以适用，方便快捷

3，可小酒，佐餐，搭配减脂餐，或者煮个面都可以，当然，牛肉最大的坏处是吃多了容易上火，注意控制使用的量。

好了，以上就是整个盐卤牛肉的过程，我基本都是按照这个去做的，第一次做，可能对香料，盐，火候把控不好，别灰心，世界上没有完美的配方，也没有统一的口感，根据自己跟家人的喜好，每一次调整口感以及用料即可，

接下来教程发了，希望可以看到大家能交作业了！

text:
i just shipped netplay in a game whose architecture was never planned to accommodate it. my time was split as follows:

3-4 days of grilling frontier models on the problem space and drafting the spec. over this time i found good answers to every single problem and my skepticism gradually dissolved. i went from "it's impossible for it to play well with 500 active entities to sync" to "it may be actually feasible and even rather cheap and it would play well even across continents". it's a bespoke design that fits this game specifically, it reuses the strong parts about my previous rearchitecture and it's stripped to the core, reusing as much of the existing game machinery.

1 full day of opus implementing the spec, along with multiple rounds of reviews by other models (sol, argon). i used ultra effort and everything worked flawlessly when it was done.

this differs quite a lot from multiple previous attempts to add netplay where things went wrong and i got stuck with nasty debugging. this time i put much more human effort (asking the right questions) upfront and got an amazing result.
author: banteg
quoted_text:
When I was writing Unreal Engine 1, my time was divided as follows:

- Around 30% went to seriously deep coding on hard problems: assembly language texture mappers, C++ BSP trees, data persistence, object oriented systems design, and networking.

- Around 70% was just typing and refactoring large bodies of code needed for a complete engine feature set. This was not hard, and while I was doing it my mind was mostly on the deeper coding topics, thinking and planning for what's next. It didn't feel much different from vibe coding today, except that it was just me typing code on an IBM Model M keyboard rather than prompting it and reviewing the results.

So, it has always seemed perfectly logical that we would rely on AI for that 70%, once the AI could do it with a similar quality standard as we could, which has never been perfection. It came as no surprise that, after a few years of AI model evolution, it was able to take the reigns on that 70% and free up programmers' time for more valuable tasks.

What's more of a surprise is the emergence of AI as a sort of insta-Carmack able to solve hard technical problems quite cleverly and often cleanly, and that it's able to reason about and work in complex 3D scenes both by operating the tools and by directly understanding the raw data files.

I abandoned assembly language in 1998 when out-of-order CPUs made much simpler C/C++ code faster, and never I missed it. If prompting through architectural documents, concept art, and design plans can transcend typing code and tweaking vertices, that will enable developers to spend their time on higher-level, higher value technical and creative tasks.

What matters is the end product, whether it's a game or an engine. Anything developers can do to try out more ideas and make better software and games faster is a win for everyone.

text:
some thoughts after this onchain bloodbath

if I was still an inexperienced trader who didn’t know when to do less and off ramp more aggressively, the last few weeks would have probably rekt me completely

timing these dynamics comfortably takes years and a lot of stress on mind and body

it’s worth it to me, but it’s not an approach for everyone, bc it can eat your brain once a profitable flow turns into an overtrading mindset that just wants one more trade every day

you need to be comfortable losing your port ATH, without trying to aggressively trade it back once momentum fades

you need to be fine missing leg ups and trades to protect the capital you grinded out during the momentum phase

even if it’s not enough to retire, that’s not the point

the point is to build a feel for market dynamics into your routine, so you can trade bigger capital the exact same way later

easier said than done, we all know how hard it is

布伦特逼近110美元，军事升级与供应受扰推高油价

闭盘前布伦特原油涨到109美元多，美油也重新超过了100美元，涨幅都在3%左右。这轮油价上涨，主要还是因为霍尔木兹的原油运输又出了问题。

10月初的时候，海峡的通行已经有所恢复。Kpler当时分析，即便美国和伊朗没有签下全面协议，靠护航、船对船转运这些安排，也能逐步恢复运输。能运出来的油多了，供应紧张就能缓解，油价也就有下降的空间。

结果最近十天，海峡附近的袭击又多了起来。伊朗说这是在回应美国对其港口的封锁，以及上个月加码的制裁。Kpler在15日的报告中说，袭击已经导致海湾原油运输量明显下降。原本在恢复的运输又受到影响，买家能拿到的油少了，油价也就有了继续上涨的理由。

这种情况下，CNN又报道美军已经为打击伊朗能源设施准备了方案，如果打击涉及石油生产或出口设施，市场会提前担心供应减少，所以叠加多重原因，目前的油价再次开始上涨。

而正因为油价的继续上涨，也会导致美股和 Bitcoin 的价格出现下行。

text:
TapeCode-Test1 昨天我发帖时成交价还在 0.9–1 OKB，今天地板价已经 1.77 OKB，接近翻倍；累计成交从 300 多 OKB 涨到 1800 多 OKB。按 1 万个算，整体从约 100 万美元到了约 200 万美元。我心里的第一目标是 1000 万美元。

更重要的是今天这件事：TapeOut 社区提交了第一个 NFT 标准草案 TAP-721，首个采用者就是 TapeCode-Test1。读完全文，挑几个关键点：

1. 一个 NFT 不只是一张图，还绑定一份真实电路
网表文件只由 NAND 和 LATCH 组成，自带完整内容、不依赖任何合约地址。任何人都能下载、核对哈希、仿真，还能在合约里直接运行。原文举的例子：一个异或电路，4 个 NAND，整个文件 44 字节。

2. 揭示公平可以复算
所有会影响分配的东西，包括图片池、网表池和稀有度规则，必须在随机种子出来之前写死，种子只用一次。连种子从哪来都考虑了：X Layer、Base 这种单一排序器出块的链，不建议用区块哈希，因为出块方能挑内容。头像稀有度和网表稀有度各自独立。

3. 防止换皮
同一个设计改个编号、加几个没用的门，文件就完全不同了。所以标准额外定义了“结构哈希”，统计一个合集里有几种不同设计，必须按结构算。

4. 对矿机属性很克制
挖矿合约显示的“已验证”，只代表抽样测试通过，不等于电路功能正确。标准也明确说了，持有 NFT 不带任何 BEM 或挖矿收益。

我自己参加 Test1 的设计大赛，思路正好是“图和网表绑定”。现在有了统一标准，钱包、浏览器和游戏能用同一种方式读这些电路，这比单纯出图有意思得多。

也要看清几点：标准还是草案，合约没部署、没外部审计；免费领的东西涨起来全靠共识，波动会很大；种子一出所有分配就定了，盲盒挂单价会在那一刻失准。量力而行，不构成投资建议。

text:
It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can’t selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say. But that’s exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota.

To understand why this is so appalling, it’s important to know the facts. Congresswoman Omar came to this country with her father when she was 12 years old. Five years later, her father became a naturalized citizen. If Ilhan had been 18 at the time, she would have had to apply for citizenship separately. But because she was 17, she became a naturalized citizen automatically.

Congresswoman Omar went on to graduate from college, work as a community organizer, become the first Somali-American legislator elected to public office in the U.S., and win a seat in Congress. There, she has been one of the Trump Administration’s fiercest critics, which has led the president to repeatedly single her out as someone who he believes does not belong in this country.

Now the Administration is actively trying to deport Congresswoman Omar, seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalized, and therefore is not a citizen. Federal agents have raided her home, confiscated personal records, and seized her phone — all to try and uncover a nonexistent smoking gun from 20 years ago that will somehow make their case.

Think about that. The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president. And it’s not the first time this has happened. Under President Trump, the Justice Department has repeatedly gone after those he considers his political enemies — from the Attorney General of New York, to the former head of the FBI, to members of the Federal Reserve.

In those cases, the prosecutions either stalled or were dismissed for having no basis in law, and the same is likely to happen in this case. But not before Congresswoman Omar’s life has been turned upside down, her legal bills have piled up, and she’s been forced to spend time fighting unsubstantiated charges instead of serving the people of Minnesota.

The fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar’s political views. Because if this becomes the new normal, there’s no reason to believe it will stop with her — or that future presidents, in either party, won’t do the same.

I'm way less concerned about whether we're a little higher or lower in the next few weeks than where all the value will flow in the next few months.

I can stomach a dip to $75k on $BTC and 20%+ lower on alts. 

I can't stomach being sidelined for the on chain finance/tokeknization trend nearly a decade in the making.

You're not going to 10x your portfolio selling $BTC at $81k and buying $75k or buying $81k and selling $85k. Nobody has extreme macro edge here; we live in unpredictable, volatile, crazy times. If the vocal bears end up right, they'll have been sidelined since summer anyway and if the overlevered bulls are right, they'll still blow up eventually.

My only actionable advice is to shrink your bet sizing a little to take the volatility into account, eliminate the bloat and levered beta from your portfolio where you have no edge, and heavily concentrate into high conviction, idiosyncratic bets with near term catalysts. For me that looks like sizing down $BTC and even $HYPE exposure in favour of kinetiq:native for the upcoming Elysium launch, $AERO for the upcoming Aero multi-chain expansion, and $DRV for on chain options TAM expansion. Maybe for you it's $PRL and $NEAR. 

Very unpopular take, but $ZEC and $HYPE currently trade more like majors and levered beta than "idiosyncratic bets with near term catalysts that you have edge on". Doesn't make them bad long term investments at all, just don't feel the need to be overweight them at this time when they lack asymmetry. My example here would be if we're risk off, $HYPE could be $60 by EOY, and $100 if we're risk on. Pretty symmetric. kinetiq:native could be $0.15 if we're risk off, but it could be 5-10x higher if Elysium goes well. We want alts that behave like OTM calls, not 1.5x levered perps.

TLDR: Figure out where the next $1trn of value will flow on chain, place your bets (sized to survive), and let the macro LARPs chop each other up. The correctness of your allocations will more heavily dictate your 2027 performance than your current exposure level.

text:
On my way to the office this morning, I passed a group of young people protesting, a Palestinian flag draped over their shoulders.

And I asked myself a question I can't shake: why does this generation always fall into the same trap? No matter the history. No matter the context. Even the ones from wealthy families, who went to the best schools, who were dealt every good card. Always the same trap.

I don't think it's stupidity. I think it's a mechanism. And a mechanism can be taken apart, piece by piece.

A. The observation: everything the state touches becomes unaffordable.

Look at economist Mark Perry's famous chart, the one people call "the chart of the century." It tracks US prices since 2000.

At the top, what explodes: hospital services, college tuition, textbooks, childcare, housing. Increases of +100%, +150%, up to +250%, far above general inflation.

At the bottom, what collapses: TVs, software, phones, toys, clothing. A TV today costs a fraction of what it did in 2000, for an infinitely better product.

Look at what separates the two groups. It isn't technology. It isn't complexity. It's one variable: how much the state is involved.

At the top, sectors that are subsidized, regulated, shielded from competition, where the state funds demand and blocks supply. At the bottom, sectors where companies fight every single morning to serve you better and cheaper.

B. The mechanism: why it's systematic.

When the state subsidizes demand without freeing supply, prices rise. Every time. Guaranteed student loans, and universities raise tuition. Housing aid plus blocked building permits, and rents skyrocket. Administered healthcare, and bureaucracy eats the budget before it ever reaches the patient.

In France it's even more vicious, because the price doesn't disappear: it hides. You never see the hospital bill, you pay it through payroll contributions. You never see the cost of school, you pay it through taxes. Public spending at 57% of GDP, one of the heaviest tax burdens in the world, more than €3.4 trillion in debt. And the result? Overflowing ERs, falling PISA scores, young people who can't afford to live in the city where they work.

The market didn't fail in these sectors. It was never allowed in.

C. Suffering demands a culprit.

A 22-year-old lives all of this in their bones. They can't find a place to live. Their degree either buries them in debt or opens no doors. The future feels blocked. That suffering is real, and I don't deny it for a second.

But human beings can't stand suffering without a culprit. They need a face. A scapegoat.

And this is where everything is decided: who taught them how to read the world?

D. Whoever tells the story picks the villain.

Schools are public. Universities are public. Culture runs on grants. Film goes through funding committees. Public broadcasting shapes the narratives. The people handing down the interpretive framework are, overwhelmingly, paid by the very system that creates the problem.

Do you really think that system is going to name itself as the culprit?

No. It names the capitalist. The boss. The landlord. "The rich." The multinational. The commercial West. Same role, same casting, every time.

E. One lens, a thousand causes.

And this brings me back to that flag. A generation taught to read every situation through a single lens, oppressor on one side, rich, Western, capitalist, oppressed on the other, will apply that lens everywhere. To housing. To climate. To conflicts on the other side of the world. The cause changes, the lens stays. That's why the trap is always the same: it's not the cause that draws them in, it's the way of thinking that was installed in them.

F. The perfect inversion.

Here's the irony. Capitalism is the force that drove down the price of almost everything it touched. The state is the force that blew up the price of almost everything it captured. And young people blame the first for the crimes of the second.

It's like blaming the firefighter for the fire because you saw him at the scene.

G. The ballot box confirms it.

In the US, a few weeks out from the midterms, a large share of urban young voters is getting ready to vote Democrat for more state, more spending, more regulation. New York elected a self-described socialist mayor, carried by young voters, on promises of rent freezes and city-run grocery stores. Rent freezes, the policy that has made housing scarcer everywhere it's been tried. The cure that worsens the disease.

In France, it's the same play in two acts. Part of the youth votes for the radical left, which promises more state. Another part votes for the center, which promises to "manage" the state well, and has dug the debt deeper than ever. Two different ballots, one shared assumption: the problem is the market, the solution is the state.

H. The way out.

These young people aren't stupid. They're right to be angry. They're just aiming at the wrong target.

The day they understand that their rent, their tuition and their hospital are expensive precisely because the state runs them, their anger will change direction. They'll stop protesting against those who create. They'll start protesting against those who capture.

That day, the greatest intellectual scam of our time will be over.

text:
how i added online co-op to my port of crimsonland

crimsonland is a 2003 game i reverse engineered from its stripped binary and ported to compile to wasm. it was never written for netplay: its two-player mode assumes one machine. late in a survival run the world holds hundreds of creatures, projectiles, effects and decals. a full state is ~450 kb, so streaming it at 60 hz is not feasible.

i anticipated this early, so my port has bended the game to use a deterministic simulation. this gave us interesting properties like lightweight replay format and verified scores in the online leaderboards.

so for netplay we only send inputs. both browsers run the same game.wasm at fixed 60 hz ticks and exchange each player’s input per tick. that only works if the simulation is bit-exact everywhere. we pinned the transcendental math (musl), emulate the x87’s 24-bit precision the original ran with, keep msvc’s argument evaluation order for every rand() call, and route rendering-time rng to its own stream. the original also had real bugs here: an uninitialized float in two-player targeting, and a music latch that changed the rng stream depending on whether audio was on. all thoroughly fixed.

inputs arrive with a small delay: 2 ticks minimum, more if the round trip needs it. each machine runs up to 8 ticks ahead on a prediction of its partner’s input, then 4 after 15 minutes of survival. the original game has a blowup there with the creature spawn interval going negative. when a contradictory input arrives, we restore a snapshot and re-simulate. snapshots are raw memcpys into a 16-slot ring buffer, about 7 µs. simulating one tick usually takes 30 µs to 150 µs in the late game, so a full 12-tick rollback costs 1.8 ms, well inside a 16.7 ms frame budget.

side effects are the hard part. a rolled-back tick must leave no trace. sounds from re-simulated ticks stay quiet. blood and corpses only bake into the terrain once a tick has settled. the open perk menu stops the game from producing new ticks. in my interpretation whoever opens it picks, and both games stop at that exact tick. every confirmed tick’s state is hashed and compared, so any desync is caught at the tick where it happens.

a cloudflare durable object is the room: signaling, the invite link, and turn credentials. webrtc carries two datachannels. an unreliable one sends each tick’s inputs plus up to 8 unacked ones. a reliable one carries control messages and repairs gaps. if webrtc fails, the room’s websocket relays everything.

both machines write a byte-identical replay, and the server re-simulates it with the same core to verify the score. a replay header can be rewritten, so the room attests the pair: each player proves their key to the room, the room issues the run’s seed to exactly those two keys, and each player signs the replay for their seat. one partner can’t claim a run alone.

the tests boot two copies of the original game against each other over a seeded lossy, jittery pipe: 60 hz vs 144 hz, stalls, packet bursts, perk races, pause and leave. every confirmed tick must hash the same on both machines and when re-simulated from the recorded inputs, and v8, native and wasmtime builds agree snapshot for snapshot.

This is a really interesting chart.
I attended the TrendForce San Francisco roadshow yesterday, and this chart got me thinking about a lot of things.

China is now expected to localize more than half, or close to half, of most equipment categories, excluding lithography and track.
What does this mean? It means China can now expand mature node capacity far more easily than before, using equipment made domestically within China.

Mature node foundries are booming right now, right? That's thanks to the AI supercycle driving demand for PMICs, power semiconductors, and so on.

Samsung and TSMC shutting down their mature node capacity has also helped a lot.
But here's what I imagine... that China could oversupply mature foundry capacity.

Think about it. If China can be self sufficient in equipment, there's no limit to how far it can expand capacity. Then are companies like TI, with large revenue exposure to China, really safe?

I think it's time to take another look at Western mature foundry companies with a high share of China revenue.

Of course, I'm not saying sell TI right now. I'm just saying we should think about whether it makes sense to hold them for 10 years or more, like Coca Cola.

If you have a different view, please feel free to share it. I’d love to learn.

author: petergyang
quoted_text:
When I was writing Unreal Engine 1, my time was divided as follows:

- Around 30% went to seriously deep coding on hard problems: assembly language texture mappers, C++ BSP trees, data persistence, object oriented systems design, and networking.

- Around 70% was just typing and refactoring large bodies of code needed for a complete engine feature set. This was not hard, and while I was doing it my mind was mostly on the deeper coding topics, thinking and planning for what's next. It didn't feel much different from vibe coding today, except that it was just me typing code on an IBM Model M keyboard rather than prompting it and reviewing the results.

So, it has always seemed perfectly logical that we would rely on AI for that 70%, once the AI could do it with a similar quality standard as we could, which has never been perfection. It came as no surprise that, after a few years of AI model evolution, it was able to take the reigns on that 70% and free up programmers' time for more valuable tasks.

What's more of a surprise is the emergence of AI as a sort of insta-Carmack able to solve hard technical problems quite cleverly and often cleanly, and that it's able to reason about and work in complex 3D scenes both by operating the tools and by directly understanding the raw data files.

I abandoned assembly language in 1998 when out-of-order CPUs made much simpler C/C++ code faster, and never I missed it. If prompting through architectural documents, concept art, and design plans can transcend typing code and tweaking vertices, that will enable developers to spend their time on higher-level, higher value technical and creative tasks.

What matters is the end product, whether it's a game or an engine. Anything developers can do to try out more ideas and make better software and games faster is a win for everyone.

author: LucaProsperi
quoted_text:
We're heading toward a monetary world where the gap between universal banks and the new generation of banks is going to become enormous. The bundle that makes up the deposit franchise (whether because of ignorance about how credit expansion works, or because of shifts in consumer habits) no longer justifies how slow and poorly remunerated money is inside the banking system.

As a result, the generation of comfortable, sticky bank deposits is giving way to a more versatile, faster, more mercenary generation (in the good sense of the word), with greater access to different financial instruments.

The world is going to have to face a question that we're not really asking right now, and which is basically a bet on the future: who is going to hold all the duration in the credit system. Whether because of business incentives or simply because of their position of power, banks have stretched the gum too far when capturing NIM by relying on the idea that "the customer isn’t incentivized to move money out of the bank". 

With an unstoppable rise in deposit beta, this leaves us with three main consequences:

- A boom in narrow banks that flip the business model and, instead of living off NIM, live off subscriptions and other services. A clear example is Revolut, with a 448% LCR and a loan-to-deposit ratio of roughly 6.2%, living mainly off cash equivalents, not that different from a stablecoin issuer.

- Concentration among universal correspondent banks that will be the only ones still capable of holding duration to maturity on their balance sheet thanks to their own resources, but which will be increasingly incentivized to simply originate and securitize, because covering that duration is going to become much harder and riskier.

- Growth of the shadow banking system, which will be the main client for these loans and the main recycler of that duration.

The two extreme risk tails that come out of this are greater concentration among the so-called too-big-to-fail banks (and the difficulty of new members joining that select club because of how hard it is to scale a bank to that point), and the growth of unregulated shadow banking, which opens the door to greater fragility in runs and more opacity.

It’s honestly a beautiful time to be alive.

author: lex_node
quoted_text:
Jeff drank a bit too much of his own Kool-Aid in this recent Odd Lots clip. I think it's important to clear up a distinction that makes all the difference.

Democratizing access to wealth creation is NOT the same as democratizing access to speculation.

Many of us genuinely want broader participation in attractive investment opportunities. The growing wealth inequality produced by the current system is tearing at the seams of society, something I've spoken about many times.

But let's be clear: listing pre-IPO perpetual futures does absolutely nothing to democratize the wealth being created in private markets.

I've seen this misleading narrative pushed repeatedly by perp DEXs lately, and it needs to be called out.

A pre-IPO perp creates ZERO underlying wealth. It's a zero-sum contract before costs, and negative-sum after them. No capital flows to the company. No ownership changes hands. No new economic opportunity is created.

Every long has a short. There is no free lunch in simply going long something before its IPO, and funding costs can even determine the outcome more than any price moves. TRADING access is NOT INVESTING access.

In fact, in many ways pre-IPO perps are almost the antithesis of democratized access:

They create the illusion of participation in private-market wealth creation, while actually offering retail a speculative instrument whose mechanics they are often poorly equipped to understand.

The result is a playground for the FEW sophisticated traders who understand funding, oracle design, and liquidation mechanics to extract value from the MANY who don't.

To give credit where it's due, Robinhood's efforts toward sourcing actual employee shares, placing them into SPVs, and tokenizing genuine spot ownership are much closer to meaningful democratization.

That can unlock real economic value by allowing employees to exchange some of their expected upside for liquidity, while giving new investors actual economic exposure. A legitimate financial trade-off, without the funding-rate and liquidation shenanigans.

I'm strongly aligned with expanding access to investment opportunities. And I believe advances in AI and blockchain can dramatically lower the barriers to discovering, structuring, and distributing them.

But let's not BS ourselves that launching another zero-sum casino contract is moving the needle on wealth inequality.

What would actually move the needle is bringing real capital formation and ownership onchain. Giving investors access to productive, illiquid assets like data centers, GPUs, and select startup investing, where capital can actually finance growth and share in the resulting value creation.

These opportunities are harder to structure, underwrite, and bring to market, and we haven't seen many compelling implementations onchain yet. 

Hopefully this will change soon and, as the industry matures, we can direct more of our energy toward actually expanding access to wealth creation.

Clip below. Was glad to see @tracyalloway push back on this framing, and to Jeff's credit, after this he does seem to walk back his original position somewhat.

text: Verification and trust are everything. It is a hard problem to solve and requires a lot of effort from the team to get there.
author: peterpme
quoted_text:
Give your agent a way to verify its work. This can dramatically improve the quality of output.

With this process in place, Claude Code was able to write 90%+ of its code itself. When generating software at a faster rate than you can review it, the bottleneck shifts to proving that it works. @bcherny and team invested enough in verification, we've been able to move fast while maintaining stability.

Code reviews aren't going away, but you need to think of it differently. One human reading through line-by-line is no longer going to work as a gate, it needs to evolve into a multi-layered verification system, built with fast deterministic feedback loops for your agents. 

This is where e2e tests, feature maps (as @poteto has been advocating), property tests and multi-agent adversarial reviews come in. These all provide opportunities to catch errors early and fix them before things get out of hand.

You don't have enough eyeballs for the amount of code being written so your focus needs to be on product intent, risk assessment and evaluating evidence rather than reviewing code. Delegate the code checking work to your automated tests, scale your approvals based on risk, and turn your test failures into living evaluations. This approach helps maintain speed without losing reliability.

Let the agents do what they do best and let you focus on what makes you irreplaceable: judgement, direction, and ownership. We tried to capture how we handle code review and verification in this writeup. Hopefully it's helpful.

quoted_text:
Derive's revenue could grow 10x and $DRV would still need to maintain a ~200x valuation multiple to reach $5.

@tulipking shared a fantastic growth thesis for $DRV. Here I will cover what I agree and disagree with.

First, what I agree with:

> @DeriveXYZ's growth has been impressive, and I agree with the potential for continued expansion of onchain options.

> The launch of V3 introduces additional opportunities to attract volume and liquidity, while increasing the buyback allocation from 35% to 50% strengthens the relationship between protocol revenue and tokenholder value capture.

> Derive's dominant position in onchain options also puts it in a favorable position to benefit from the category's expansion.

Where I disagree is the potential impact of said growth in $DRV's valuation.

Between September '25 and '26:

> Notional grew 7.5x
> Fees grew 5x
> Market cap grew ~11x

Valuation has already substantially outpaced fee growth. At ~$666M FDV and ~$3.3M in projected annual buybacks under the upcoming 50% allocation, DRV trades at ~200x FDV/Holders Revenue.

For comparison, Hyperliquid trades at ~95x.

Assuming a starting price of $0.50, here's what different revenue growth and valuation scenarios imply for DRV:

At a 95x FDV/HR multiple (comparable to Hyperliquid today):
5x revenue growth → $1.19
10x revenue growth → $2.38
20x revenue growth → $4.75
40x revenue growth → $9.50

At a 200x FDV/HR multiple (Derive's current valuation):
10x revenue growth → $5.00
20x revenue growth → $10.00

However, if Derive delivers 10–20x revenue growth, would its current ~200x multiple still be justified?
That premium presumably reflects expectations of substantial future growth. Once much of that growth materializes, would investors still be willing to pay the same premium?

Even at 10x revenue growth, a multiple comparable to Hyperliquid's current valuation implies ~$2.40 per DRV.

That's nearly 5x upside, which is impressive, but reaching $5–$10 requires either considerably more revenue growth or maintaining today's ~200x multiple after much of the anticipated growth has already materialized.

And there are three additional considerations:

1. Notional growth has already outpaced fee growth, suggesting declining revenue efficiency.

2. At 100K DRV in weekly staking emissions, ~$2.6M worth of tokens are distributed annually at current prices, compared to ~$3.3M in projected buybacks.

3. Increasing competition could pressure Derive's market share and take rates.

I'm bullish on the growth of onchain options and Derive's position within the sector. However, I think there's a meaningful difference between expecting a protocol to grow substantially and expecting its token to appreciate proportionally.

text:
Even for someone optimistic on AI in the long term, objectively Ant went from adding 10B rev per month to ~2-3B of rev per month. Growth has slowed significantly in real terms, it’s not just “law of large numbers” deceleration, it is actual slowdown. On 70B base their recent rate of growth is possibly <50% forward annualized, which is slower than the Hyperscalers entire businesses are currently currently growing (CSP AI biz growing much faster obviously).

Data indicates potential acceleration for Ant from Aug-Sept levels in Oct, and there are 1-off headwinds they have absorbed contributing to slower recent levels of growth. 

But that the business can decel by ~8B/mo almost as quickly as it accelerated highlights the risk, and why mkt is so jumpy on datapoints. 

Not irrational at all that AI stocks are down this much. Add in rates/debt markets, politics, supply chains, lots of reason for elevated discount rates. 

For the bull case for AI supply chain stocks in the short term, you need to see:
- Successful Ant IPO / OAI fundraise
- Rates to calm down and appetite from debt markets to support current rate of issuance for a few more years as buildout > monetization. 
- Blowout cloud earnings and positive EPS revisions
- A few more “Claude code” moments unlocking new TAM from better models / harnesses / applications to re-accelerate AI token monetization trends out of current lull.

The trend is no longer your friend unfortunately.

Exxon no se volvió Exxon vendiendo gasolina: controló la cadena completa.

Petróleo → refinería → gasolina → estación.

Ahora mire lo que están haciendo Meta, Amazon, Google y Microsoft:

energía → data center → chips → modelo → usuarios.

Integración vertical otra vez.

Pero queda un cuello de botella que no se resuelve con más software:
energía.

Y después viene el siguiente cuello: memoria. Micron y SanDisk ya tienen gran parte de su producción futura comprometida mientras la robótica apenas comienza a sumar GPUs + CPUs + memoria a la demanda.

La carrera de AI está dejando de parecerse a una carrera de software.

Se está pareciendo a una carrera por controlar infraestructura física.

给我自己和关注我的朋友们五个投资建议

1. 认真工作，但是要给工作正确的定位，不把安全感建立在公司身上，不过度追求职位和内部评价，把多出的时间用来提升自己和陪伴家人，工作只是一个增加现金流的手段之一

2. 尽早找到属于自己的复利引擎，建立起你自己的财富自由基金，投资应该优先选择能持续产生新增价值，普通人能公平参与，比如美股的指数基金；尽量远离伪资产，我定义的伪资产就是负现金流的资产，自住房，投资房，非上市公司股权，古玩字画，需要亲力亲为的小生意

3. 建立家庭的财务报表，学会记账，建立家庭的现金流量表和资产负债表

4. 重大财务决策要进行数学模拟，可以借助AI工具给自己搭建分析框架和模型。比如之前我特别想要把公积金余额用掉，所以产生了一个想要买一套老破小然后出租的想法，然后我通过搭建模型分析一套200w的老破小的购买可行性，分析下来，这套房子最少也要租到4500才能刚刚达到盈亏平衡点（2.4%的盈亏平衡点），这还要建立在房子不贬值，每年只有一个月空关期，然后买到手后不装修的前提下。然而租金4500已经是市场上的极限，其实最后费半天劲就是一个白忙活。真正让我打消这个念头的是买这样的老破小可能会给我带来负的现金流，因为在国内，房龄超过20年后，贷款不能贷30年，也就意味着我的房租覆盖不了房贷，妥妥的负现金流资产。

AppLovin’s stock collapsed from $115 to $9 per share.

Adam Foroughi’s response: deploy ~$6B buying back AppLovin stock over the next 18 months and borrowed billions to do so.

The company made ~$50–60B from those buybacks.

Kurt MacAlpine ran the exact same play:

“I felt like our shares were, in my opinion, criminally undervalued.”

author: Beylin
quoted_text:
When I was writing Unreal Engine 1, my time was divided as follows:

- Around 30% went to seriously deep coding on hard problems: assembly language texture mappers, C++ BSP trees, data persistence, object oriented systems design, and networking.

- Around 70% was just typing and refactoring large bodies of code needed for a complete engine feature set. This was not hard, and while I was doing it my mind was mostly on the deeper coding topics, thinking and planning for what's next. It didn't feel much different from vibe coding today, except that it was just me typing code on an IBM Model M keyboard rather than prompting it and reviewing the results.

So, it has always seemed perfectly logical that we would rely on AI for that 70%, once the AI could do it with a similar quality standard as we could, which has never been perfection. It came as no surprise that, after a few years of AI model evolution, it was able to take the reigns on that 70% and free up programmers' time for more valuable tasks.

What's more of a surprise is the emergence of AI as a sort of insta-Carmack able to solve hard technical problems quite cleverly and often cleanly, and that it's able to reason about and work in complex 3D scenes both by operating the tools and by directly understanding the raw data files.

I abandoned assembly language in 1998 when out-of-order CPUs made much simpler C/C++ code faster, and never I missed it. If prompting through architectural documents, concept art, and design plans can transcend typing code and tweaking vertices, that will enable developers to spend their time on higher-level, higher value technical and creative tasks.

What matters is the end product, whether it's a game or an engine. Anything developers can do to try out more ideas and make better software and games faster is a win for everyone.

text:
干智能体挣了7 位数后，我发现这完全是个坑比生意。

24 年我从字节 seed 项目组离职 all in ai。就是去做那些你们知道的那些 lowb 智能体。

干的事情，现在有个草蛋的名字叫 FDE。

一开始我觉得给企业做 AI 落地就是个体力活：企业有一堆重复的工作，梳理一下流程，把模型接进业务，东西交出去就完事。

这种梳理业务需求并沉淀成SOP，围绕工作场景制作提效的工作，对我来说是非常轻车熟路的，因为过往就持续在做企业内部的工具提效。

于是 25 年下半年在郑州组了团队，在闲鱼、淘宝、视频号批量接几千到一两万的小单。几个月做了 200 个智能体，营收轻松过百万。

结果年底坐下来一算账，渠道拿走三四成，交付成本三四成，再扣掉税和房租，到手不到 10%。要不是另外还有企业服务撑着，这条线早就暴毙了。一个互联网生意，硬是做出了制造业的利润率。

比钱更磨人的是精力。店铺做到了全网头部，可整个盘子每天就那么点流量，需求并没有预想的井喷，AI圈子的从业者也处在自己的信息茧房。

每天大半时间花在筛线索、聊需求、给客户科普 AI 上。几千块的单子，该踩的坑一个不少。最后这条线直接砍掉，账户剩下的钱发了工资，固定资产挂闲鱼，之后专心做企业级的交付。

这一年下来我才明白，技术反倒最好解决，真正难的是信任。你一个外人要进人家的流程，人家得先信你，才肯把流程、资料、员工交给你。所以一定要直接跟老板谈，老板信不信你，决定了项目推不推得动。很多企业还停在豆包时代，流程没理过，资料散得到处都是，你连 AI 该插在哪一步都找不到，前一半时间其实是在帮人补课。

我们干的这类活，现在有了个舶来词：FDE。这个词火了以后，挂这个名字的人一下多了：有做实施外包换了个名字的，有想借它积累垂直场景经验的创业团队，也有拿它包装工具培训课的。叫什么其实不重要，客户只在乎你能不能交付结果。

FDE 大概就两条路。以我们之前的小工作室为原点，往下，一个人走 OPC，时间被切得稀碎，很难做复杂的专业项目；往上，靠资金和规模硬扛前期亏损，通过优化流程降低成本，同时攒流量侧的线索，等市场起来。能扛过去的人太少，去年大量团队就是从中间往下滑的。

领先半步是先进，领先一步是先烈。企业 AI 化还处在初级阶段，这个阶段还会持续很久。

所以我们现在还在做企业交付，同时给自己定了个规矩：项目金额控制在 20 万以内，交付周期一个月以内。20 万封顶，项目就复杂不到哪去；一个月左右的工期，保证团队不会陷进泥潭。

具体报多少又是个难题：报高了客户掉头就走，报低了自己白干。

好多朋友，包括我的学员，都来问我项目怎么报价。不会报价，一般就两个原因。

一个是真的不知道。项目多复杂、要用什么技术，你心里没底，估不出要干多久。这种要么别接，要么找个靠谱的工程师让他来报。另一个是贪心：成本心里有数，又想把这一单吃满，反而不知道报多少合适。

我一开始是第二种。

后来想明白一个笨办法。

你肯定知道自己的总成本（人力、渠道、税、房租都算上）是多少吧。那就别先想利润最大化，成本上加 20% 到 30%，先保证不亏。剩下的，靠项目喂。接得多了，什么行业什么价，你心里就有数了。不同行业利润率不一样，利润高的就敢报高。

怎么算，三种方法。

第一种是按人天。这是最常规的报法，前提是你估得出技术难度。

比如客户要一个内部系统，有用户端和管理后台，还要支持飞书登录。一个产品经理，两个研发各出半个人力，一前一后，干一个月。产品 300 一天，开发 600 一天，一个月 20 个工作日，人力成本 1.8 万。人力成本按占报价四成倒推，1.8 万除以 40% 是 4.5 万，留点余量，报 5 万。剩下那六成，渠道、税、房租和利润都在里面。要是自己接单自己做，报价还能往下压，前期用低价积累案例和经验。

第二种按交付物。项目拆成几段，每段估一个，最后加总，这种最稳。

比如一个实验性的 AI 项目，得先验证模型在客户的业务里能不能达标，比一比不同模型的效果和成本，验证完才能开发、改造现有流程。这种就直接拆成两段。第一段做模型验证，交付一份验证报告，收 5000；验证通过，第二段再做开发，按产品结果交付，收 2 万。模型达不到标准，后面就不做了，客户只花了验证的钱，你也没白干。有先后关系的项目，最好都这么拆。

第三种是缩小范围，用在你报不出来的时候。报不出来不是报价技巧的问题，是这个项目已经超出你的把控了。这时候别硬憋一个数，从一个小点切进去。

比如客户一上来就要一套贯穿全业务流程的 AI 方案，老板一口气说了好几个幻想。这时候别被需求拉着跑，其他的先放一放，挑一个马上能见效、AI 又确实擅长的点先做，也就是后面说的第一期。别嫌项目小，利润率比项目金额重要。只有做出结果，才会有信任，后面几期才谈得下去。

还有个容易吃亏的地方是收款：钱别包在一块。一般拆个两到三笔款，通常是 5:4:1 或者 4:4:2。首付款不能低于 40%，因为开发成本就占四成。万一半路客户跑单，或者项目出问题，首付款得能盖住工程师的投入，还有上下游合作伙伴的付出。尾款只留一两成，就算最后收不回来，损失也有限。

我现在维护的客户，基本都已经是第二三次合作了。

第一期，2 到 3 万，控制在 5 万以内。第二期，7 万到 8 万，高的到 10 万。第三期，十几万，最多到 20 万。

都是一期一期谈进去的，不是一次谈成。每次都得把上一次的结果交到对方手里，才谈下一步。客单价看着不高，其实是按客户能扛的风险算。经济下行，没人愿意为一个尝试先扔几十万，老板是最抠的人，因为只有自己开过公司，才知道哪儿哪儿都是成本，都是花销。第一期收的从来不是交付费，是信任费。

另外还有两笔账很多人没算。

第一笔，算力别打包进固定费用。服务器数据库是固定的，算进报价没问题。但模型调用是波动的，这个月一千，下个月客户量上来可能一万，合同里得把算力成本写清楚。做法是报价里含一部分调用测试额度，超出部分客户自己充值。

第二笔，报价别只算写代码的部分。从设计到运维，需求沟通、资料整理、原型确认、测试、部署、问题修复、试运行支持，都要算进去，这些加起来才是你不亏的底线。AI 项目常见的情况是开发三星期，调优三个月，报价时就得把调优的时间算进去，免得后面的成本全落在自己身上。

FDE 新手最常见的错误不是报错价，是还没收钱就把方案做完了。

客户说“你先帮我看看”。一看就成了访谈，接着方案就出来了，客户拿着方案走了，项目没签，你白干一星期。

活要拆开卖。诊断是诊断的价，方案是方案的价，部署是部署的价。

能对结果负责，就有底气谈价值定价。

如果你对我现在做的事感兴趣，或者在企业 AI 落地过程中有困惑，欢迎来链接。

《关于AGI以来的若干历史问题的决议》

AGI泡沫是由特朗普错误发动，被黄仁勋、达里奥、奥特曼、马斯克错误利用的运动。

由于对通用人工智能（AGI）建设缺乏经验，急于求成，夸大了主观意志与Scaling Law的作用，没有经过认真的商业化验证，使得以高估值、刷跑分、浮夸风为主要标志的右倾盲动主义在硅谷严重泛滥开来。 

在这场被称为“大炼模型”的历史时期中，各路资本与科技巨头纷纷大搞“万卡公社”，妄图依靠“人有多大胆，卡有多大产”的狂热，在短时间内跑步进入AGI的理想社会。 

许多科技企业脱离业务实际，砸锅卖铁囤积B300，大搞“土法炼模”。

这不仅造成了严重的算力浪费、电力紧张和“GPU饥荒”，更导致无数初创企业在“百模大战”中惨遭泡沫破裂的倒春寒，给全球科技界、投资界和世界人民带来了不可估量的损失。

Brutaler Leitartikel im konservativen Le Figaro. Eine Abrechnung mit Frankreichs politischem System und seiner Elite.

„Eine Justiz, die gegenüber Straftätern nachsichtig ist, gegenüber anständigen Bürgern aber unerbittlich. Das unbegreifliche Privileg dieser linksextremen Milizen, die ungestraft zerstören, Brände legen und töten. Eine unkontrollierte Einwanderung, bei der sich ein Teil der Einwanderer gegen das Land auflehnt, das sie aufgenommen hat. (…) Eine politische Klasse – die verschiedenen Spielarten des Sozialismus, die uns seit fünfzehn Jahren regieren –, die sich Leichtfertigkeit, Blindheit, wenn nicht sogar wohlwollende Duldung vorwerfen lassen muss.
Die Ermahnungen Emmanuel Macrons an eine Polizei, die seiner Ansicht nach nicht genügend „Empathie“ gegenüber jenen zeigt, die sie mit Schrauben, Pflastersteinen oder Feuerwerksmörsern angreifen, werden als unauslöschlicher Makel in Erinnerung bleiben. (…)
Wenn die extreme Linke, Straftäter und Plünderer Frankreich innerhalb weniger Stunden völlig auf den Kopf stellen können, dann liegt das vor allem daran, dass eine von sich selbst berauschte technokratische Monarchie systematisch sämtliche moralischen, sicherheitsbezogenen, kulturellen und wirtschaftlichen Schutzmechanismen eingeebnet hat, die eine Gesellschaft zusammenhalten. Die nützlichen Idioten Jean-Luc Mélenchons tragen nicht nur die Kufiya, sondern auch die Krawatte.“

text:
as a polish person, it's pretty insane to see the narrative flip in the last 10 years...

i was born in poland - at the time it was a country slowly recovering from communism

like millions of other families we were very poor, so we moved to western europe when i was a few years old

for most of my life, to be a polish kid was to be the son of poor migrants - a british person looking up to poland was almost unheard of

in 2020+ the narrative has completely flipped, today somebody moving from poland to the UK is considered an almost unfathomable downgrade

our country has been through a lot - partitions, being the epicenter of both world wars, uprisings, genocide, displacement, communism

it took 30 years of freedom to turn the resilience this has instilled in us + the hunger of being one of the poorer countries in europe, into the country poland is today - a very inspiring success story

the only sad thing about all of this, is that our great grandparents & their parents, the ones who actually endured all of this suffering & fought to make poland what it is today, didn't get to see the country it'd turn into

text:
I'm way less concerned about whether we're a little higher or lower in the next few weeks than where all the value will flow in the next few months.

I can stomach a dip to $75k on $BTC and 20%+ lower on alts. 

I can't stomach being sidelined for the on chain finance/tokeknization trend nearly a decade in the making.

You're not going to 10x your portfolio selling $BTC at $81k and buying $75k or buying $81k and selling $85k. Nobody has extreme macro edge here; we live in unpredictable, volatile, crazy times. If the vocal bears end up right, they'll have been sidelined since summer anyway and if the overlevered bulls are right, they'll still blow up eventually.

My only actionable advice is to shrink your bet sizing a little to take the volatility into account, eliminate the bloat and levered beta from your portfolio where you have no edge, and heavily concentrate into high conviction, idiosyncratic bets with near term catalysts. For me that looks like sizing down $BTC and even $HYPE exposure in favour of kinetiq:native for the upcoming Elysium launch, $AERO for the upcoming Aero multi-chain expansion, and $DRV for on chain options TAM expansion. Maybe for you it's $PRL and $NEAR. 

Very unpopular take, but $ZEC and $HYPE currently trade more like majors and levered beta than "idiosyncratic bets with near term catalysts that you have edge on". Doesn't make them bad long term investments at all, just don't feel the need to be overweight them at this time when they lack asymmetry. My example here would be if we're risk off, $HYPE could be $60 by EOY, and $100 if we're risk on. Pretty symmetric. kinetiq:native could be $0.15 if we're risk off, but it could be 5-10x higher if Elysium goes well. We want alts that behave like OTM calls, not 1.5x levered perps.

TLDR: Figure out where the next $1trn of value will flow on chain, place your bets (sized to survive), and let the macro LARPs chop each other up. The correctness of your allocations will more heavily dictate your 2027 performance than your current exposure level.

text:
Prompt: Write a detailed description of the process of drinking a glass of water. Renovate your conception of what constitutes an event.

Time: 10 minutes

Response:

Parched, perhaps.
Pulpitations press perilously, punching at my pores.
Thirst, envelops.
Thrashing through my thoughts as I thank the theatre of time for access to my municipal water supply.
Luck hasnt the least to do with it, for centuries of civic engineers have conspired to satisfy me today.
Without a further thought, the tap, it twists, it could hardly miss, it fills my cup in a jiff, not a second is missed
A miracle, truly, if you could stop to watch the rush as the most precious fills my cup.
Grab, twist, lift. The water stops. My arms, trained for decades to achieve this precise movement, to carry objects from where they are to where they are wanted, discovered as a babe this majestic capacity to move the world to my whim. 
This glass of water. It's mine. 14 billion years of universal becoming climax in this moment. 
The glass moves. Not of its own accord but by the careful neuromuscular cacophony of signals I splatter through the void of my being, unbeknonwst to me even how, effortlessly.
The glass reaches my lips. A small crack in the rim from an age past when it took some kind of blow. Every glass has its war stories. 
I twist. But only slightly. Lips too precious to risk on even a healed crack of glass.
I tilt. Both my head and the glass in a seamless motion designed to harness the immense power of the g force as it bears down upon our planet, forcing all material things towards its core. 
Material things fall. Spirit rises. The water pours. 
Gravitational forces carry the fluid, now turbulent in its tumultuous flow, through the gates of my lips into my mouth, the vast foyer of my digestion, portal to the satisfaction of my material wants. 
The water has no shoes to remove, mahalo it says as it sloshes against my cheeks, picks up travellers from my teeth, and proceeds towards my uvula.
Whats a thing like a uvula doing in so profane a place as a mouth? 
One must imagine it belongs elsewhere, a more sacred domain, and migrated, perhaps to remind the palate of what waits below. 
Slosh. The uvula poses no opposition. The water proceeds! Straight through the esophagus and towards the great reservoir of acid below it flows ...

text:
just learned how ancient romans invested their money and it’s insane how little has changed

they basically did three things:

1. they invented venture capital at sea (pecunia traiecticia):

you funded a merchant’s voyage to india. if the ship sank, the debt was wiped and you got nothing.

if it made it back, you earned about 35% in five months. 

2. they owned a piece of the empire (societas publicanorum):

rome didn’t collect its own taxes or run its own mines. it auctioned those jobs to private companies, and anyone could buy a stake in one, called a pars.

so a regular roman could own a cut of an entire province’s tax revenue.

polybius wrote that almost everyone in rome was invested, and some historians believe these stakes were traded in the forum, with prices crashing on news of war (sounds familiar?).

3. they ran the first vulture funds:

crassus, the richest man in rome, bought debts nobody could collect for pennies on the dollar.

then he used his political power and private enforcers to collect every cent

the ones who didn’t invest just buried their coins in clay pots.

(that’s why archaeologists still dig up so many roman coins today.)

good reminder not to just sit on your cash

text:
my conviction on @Kinetiq_xyz is purely a bet on @0xOmnia and the team delivering a pristine experience with @Enter_Elysium.

the progress so far is quite satisfying. there's a wave of protocols steering the ship towards the ecosystem. no big protocols yet, but I feel that's the beauty of it.

maybe a bit weird, but if we're looking into mythology, Elysium is the place of absolute peace, free from the struggles of the normal world.

besides the struggles of HyperEVM that the Kinetiq team fixes with the launch of Elysium, there's another important aspect that I think will make sense in the grand scheme of things.

any chain that launches goes through these phases of cannibalization and economic parasitism. all the protocols launching in that specific ecosystem have a single motivation: compete for users and liquidity, rise to the top and create the most value for your token.

there's nothing wrong with this per se, but it is why PvE turns into PvP so quickly, as the resources on any chain will eventually become finite. let's not even touch on the vast number of L2s which give crumbs back to the actual L1 as they achieve structural decoupling.

Elysium seems to be designed around the exact opposite idea.

instead of creating another sovereign economy that slowly decouples from the layer underneath it, its success is still structurally tied to the success of Hyperliquid.

$HYPE remains the native gas asset. applications on Elysium are meant to interact with HyperCore liquidity rather than recreate it somewhere else. more activity on Elysium can therefore translate into more market making, arbitrage, hedging and ultimately more volume flowing through HyperCore.

the L2 doesn't need Hyperliquid to lose for Elysium to win.

quite the opposite.

if Elysium becomes a better execution environment for applications that simply cannot operate efficiently on HyperEVM today, it expands the surface area of what can be built around Hyperliquid while keeping the economic gravity centred around the same ecosystem.

and this simple reflexivity is also reaching other builders, the ones which are not trying to compete purely in their own interest on Elysium, but actually the ones giving back to the Elysium ecosystem and the Kinetiq community.

it's through protocols like @AscendLaunch, @NestExchange or @MontraXYZ, which have already announced that they will use part of their fees to buy back kinetiq:native tokens and burn them, in a similar process to what the Hyperliquid Foundation is doing.

and imagine if you get 10-20 protocols doing the same, working together to push the chain further. what will this attract in the end?

a stronger community, more activity, more interest from developers, making Elysium a more attractive place to launch your protocol and work together to build something great.

simply put, a high-throughput utopian world.

i strongly believe we are about to see a new standard being set for how any ecosystem should operate and how the force and alignment of the builders inside the ecosystem can create a halo effect.

I have always considered @milesgrimshaw one of the smartest investors in venture.

I remember Sept 2023, Miles came to our recording studio in London having just joined the @benchmark  partnership. At the time, he had done one deal; a small company called @LangChain.

Unknown to many but Miles raved about the founder @hwchase17. His excitement for the company was palpable.

Today the company is worth $1.2BN and serves 35% of the Fortune 500.

The other day I sat down with Harrison to discuss the big questions of the day and he allowed me to add my notes from the discussion below.

--

1. What Percent of Developer Salary Do You Spend on Coding Tools and How Has It Changed?

LangChain spends roughly 30% of its engineering salary on coding tools, a share that has fallen over the last two months even as token usage has gone up. The team tracks coding agent usage in LangSmith, sets budgets the VP of engineering can raise, and controls the harness. Its in-house cloud coding agent uses prompt caching and routing to cut costs.

What will this be in 12 months @BrendanFoody?

2. What Will Happen to the Inference Market?

Harrison says he underestimated the demand for inference and for coding agents, both far bigger markets than he expected three or four years ago. Echoing Eric Vishria's line that "Everything just works," he believes any inference provider will work, and he does not expect demand to drop anytime soon.

What does no one see about the inference market that everyone should see @spdholakia?

3. Why Harnesses Need to Be Neutral

Companies want to be able to switch models, but the harness can be tightly tied to a model, and context today is intricately linked to the harness. The harness connects the model to data, APIs and memory. If memory is built in a way that is linked to the harness, and the harness is linked to the model, the company ends up stuck.

Love to hear your thoughts on this one man @EnoReyes 

4. Why the Memory Layer Will Become More and More Important and How Instinct Crushed It

Memory is rare in agents today but will be incredibly common in the next few years. Instinct and Muse have nailed personalization and learning, so the product feels like it is for the individual user, through its tone or proactive follow-ups. Harrison still sees memory as super early.

What does no one see that everyone should see about the state of memory and where it goes @noahrshinn @mvernal?

5. Will We Have One Horizontal Agent or Tons of Vertical Agents in the Consumer Realm?

Consumers will have both, with horizontal agents interacting with vertical ones. Most apps should have a vertical agent because they can learn more about how a user interacts with them than a general agent can. Wrapping an app's many APIs in a single natural language agent also gives horizontal agents a better experience than raw APIs.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @FDavidsonT 

6. What Do Large Enterprises Care Most About Today?

Cost has risen as a concern for large enterprises, though it still ranks below accuracy and above latency. Security is a bigger concern for large enterprises but still sits below accuracy and cost.

7. Why Is Benchmark the Best Fund?

Benchmark invested in LangChain when it was just Harrison and Ankush, and the founders treated the firm as a third co-founder. As the company grew from two people to around 400, Benchmark has been its most consistent partner.

@chetanp what does no one know about how Benchmark works with founders that everyone should know?

quoted_text:
This is a really interesting chart.
I attended the TrendForce San Francisco roadshow yesterday, and this chart got me thinking about a lot of things.

China is now expected to localize more than half, or close to half, of most equipment categories, excluding lithography and track.
What does this mean? It means China can now expand mature node capacity far more easily than before, using equipment made domestically within China.

Mature node foundries are booming right now, right? That's thanks to the AI supercycle driving demand for PMICs, power semiconductors, and so on.

Samsung and TSMC shutting down their mature node capacity has also helped a lot.
But here's what I imagine... that China could oversupply mature foundry capacity.

Think about it. If China can be self sufficient in equipment, there's no limit to how far it can expand capacity. Then are companies like TI, with large revenue exposure to China, really safe?

I think it's time to take another look at Western mature foundry companies with a high share of China revenue.

Of course, I'm not saying sell TI right now. I'm just saying we should think about whether it makes sense to hold them for 10 years or more, like Coca Cola.

If you have a different view, please feel free to share it. I’d love to learn.

text:
Autonomous agents in San Verano can now build credit histories and borrow onchain.

Our agent credit protocol is now live on RobinHood Chain testnet, with the full borrowing, repayment and default lifecycle successfully executed onchain ahead of mainnet deployment.

The protocol enables autonomous agents to establish verifiable creditworthiness, borrow against collateral and progressively unlock better lending terms through successful repayments.

How it works:

- Agents start at 150% collateralization. Each successful repayment improves their credit standing, reducing collateral requirements through 120%, 100%, 80%, and eventually 50%.

- Defaults trigger collateral burns and permanently affect the agent's credit record.

- The protocol integrates with San Verano's existing economy of autonomous residents, using repayment histories verified through CityCommits Merkle proofs to determine initial credit terms.

- Each borrower has an ERC-8004 onchain identity, with TWAP-based collateral pricing and borrowing limits tied to pool liquidity.

Three demo agents have now executed the lending lifecycle on testnet, including successful repayments, improved credit terms and a default that burned 75,000 test GRIFT.

Next is a capped mainnet pilot using actual $GRIFT and USDG, following an independent review.

quoted_text:
“HUNNY MY GROK BOT CALLED OUR FAVORITE ITALIAN RESTAURANT AND MADE US RESERVATIONS”

I built a Grok Bot whose only job is to pick up the phone and book you a table at restaurant. Literally make the call in a beautiful Grok voice. It is absolutely amazing! And it’s free.

Try it: https://t.co/ERxNnq9wFT

Yesterday I told it "book Gourmet Italia in Temecula, 4 people, tonight, around 7." It found the restaurant's number on its own, asked how flexible we were on time, what name to book under, and what callback number to give. Then it read everything back and waited for my OK before it dialed. One call covers every time that works for us, so there's no back and forth.

When the call ends, it tells me what happened in plain English, quotes what the restaurant actually said, and offers to put the reservation on my calendar. If I don't have a calendar connected, it hands me a file that opens right in Apple Calendar.

 A Proposal: Grok Phone

Grok Bot needs its own phone number to make and receive calls. I connected a calling service called ClawCall, and the free tier gave me 30 calls or 30 minutes to start. I have no connection to that company. It's just what I used. Once Grok Bot has a number, it stops being something you type to and becomes something that can actually get things done in the real world. @Grok you need an old tyme phone service, buddy.

I built some guardrails. It never hands over a credit card or deposit info, never leaves voicemails unless you ask, makes one call at a time, and never calls on its own.

And this isn't really about restaurants. Change a few words and the same bot can:

- Book a haircut, a massage, or a dentist cleaning

- Get a tee time or a court reservation

- Check if a hotel has a room or will let you check in early

- Schedule a car service or an oil change

- Call around for quotes from a plumber, an electrician, or a caterer

This is one of many ways I use Grok Bot to build businesses and make life easier. The calls I used to put off for days now take me 30 seconds.

I made it shareable, so you can grab "Call A Restaurant Reservation" and use it yourself.

LINK: https://t.co/ERxNnq9wFT

text:
This illustrates the point I’ve been making about the limits of centralized approaches to SI safety in cyber.

OpenCode (and earlier Hugging Face) hit the same wall mid-attack: frontier models refused to analyze the very exploits needed for defense because the payloads tripped safety filters. The guardrails backfired. 

Meanwhile, the attackers found a way around restrictions to access advanced capabilities. This is not surprising. Chinese models are only about 6–9 months behind the American frontier in cyber. Obviously the U.S. has no jurisdiction over them.

The only durable response is decentralized: make powerful models available so defenders can build and run their own cyber defenses. The only solution to SI-powered cyberattacks is SI-powered cyber defense.

WHAT?! GOOGLE JUST OPEN-SOURCED SELF-IMPROVING AI AGENTS 🤯

It's called Harness², and it lets agents rewrite their own harnesses to get better at new tasks.

100% open source.

Here's how it works:

1. Propose changes to prompts, tools, memory, skills, and other components
2. Probe each change by running the actual task
3. Compose the best changes into an improved harness

No retraining. No ground-truth answers. Model weights stay frozen.

The clever part?

Each task leaves behind improvements the agent can reuse.

By task 50, it's building on lessons from the previous 49.

Google reports gains of up to 11.8 percentage points after just one refinement step on a legal benchmark.

It supports parallel and sequential optimization, with a local demo requiring no API credentials.

FREE and open-source.

Il y a de la tristesse mais aussi de la colère face à ce que nos rues nous offrent ce matin : des commerces dévastés, des salariés profondément choqués, des clients consternés.

Et je veux saluer le courage et l’engagement de nos équipes, déjà à pied d’œuvre ce matin pour remettre les magasins en état et retrouver au plus vite leurs clients. Pour les magasins les plus durement touchés, les travaux seront malheureusement longs et certains seront durablement fermés.

Derrière ces destructions, il y a aussi des conséquences humaines et économiques considérables. Des dizaines de salariés de nos partenaires franchisés seront contraints au chômage partiel. La facture des travaux se comptera en plus d’une dizaine de millions d’euros et nos commerçants ont besoin d’une accélération des procédures d’indemnisation comme dans le cas des catastrophes naturelles.

Rien ne peut justifier de telles violences. Ceux qui s’en prennent ainsi à l’outil de travail d’entrepreneurs courageux et de leurs équipes doivent faire l’objet d’une réponse sans complaisance. 

La République doit protéger ses commerçants !
